title: chore(ci): refresh the Test Core shard-timings dataset

shard split. Opened automatically by `.github/workflows/shard-timings-refresh.yml`.
Every byte came out of `scripts/measure-test-shard-timings.mjs`; nothing here was
hand-edited, and no bound, timeout or matrix entry was touched.

## What the seat landing this PR does

File nothing from this refresh's readings: no rise and no file was judged. The refusal above
is a defect in this lane, and that is the one card to file.

## Source

Measured across 6 accumulated run(s) of the 4-hourly `schedule` run of CI on
`main` — the full-battery run (#16467). A `push` run on `main` is affected-only and
is not a measurement of the workspace, so no push run feeds this file.

No single green run measures the whole workspace either — turbo's cache is namespaced
per shard and only main pushes write it, so a
package whose inputs have not changed is a HIT and the generator refuses hits rather
than recording a replay as a duration. Runs are therefore accumulated, each fenced by
its own `--run` group, until every package has been EXECUTED by at least the
generator's minimum number of them, and each weight is the median of those executions.

- https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/42538563866

- Newest run in the set: `42559743988`, commit `8dbb4a12af108f64fbc4c35b08c95af5f3e50c91` — the date this refresh carries.
- Every run above had every `Test Core (N/M)` shard job conclude `success` with its
  run-summary artifact still retained; runs that were cancelled, failed or had lost
  their artifacts were rejected by name in the log before any of these were used.

All 82 package weights were measured in these runs; nothing was carried.

⚠️ This PR references #16173 and #16222 but does NOT carry a closing keyword for them,
because a weekly lane cannot know which cards a given run ought to retire. If this is
the first refresh to land, retire those two by hand as part of merging it.

Every package carries a ceiling.

⚠️ 32 package(s) ran OVER their held ceiling in this window (marked in the table): a reading, not a red -- under #22949 ruling E the ceiling reports on every event, and a regression is judged by the diff at the top of this body. This refresh does not raise them; that takes a ruling.

## The partitioner's own pins RED on this refresh — read this before merging

This is the designed behaviour, not a defect in the refresh: the acceptance bound is
a ratio, and a package that has grown past what the Test Core split can bin makes the
pins fail with the arithmetic in the message. The remedy the partitioner names is to
raise the file-level slice count for that package — ⛔ never to raise the bound, and
⛔ never to hand-edit this dataset. This workflow deliberately does neither: it
reports and stops, because both are decisions.

Pushed and opened as the fleet App (`objectstack-fleet[bot]`, #25936), so this PR's
own events start CI: no push or reopen is needed to get its checks.

Refs #16464, #16173, #16222.
